`VrpSolver.java` has a defect in its OR-Tools pickup-delivery disjunction modeling. The call `routing.addDisjunction(new long[]{pickupIdx, deliveryIdx}, penalty)` registers BOTH the pickup and delivery nodes as a single disjunction. Combined with `addPickupAndDelivery(pickupIdx, deliveryIdx)`, this makes the `PARALLEL_CHEAPEST_INSERTION` first-solution strategy unable to construct any feasible initial solution containing the PDP pair. As a result, OR-Tools always starts GLS from an "all-dropped" state, and вЂ” because the disjunction penalty (1,000,000) is paid once per pair and the GLS time limit (3-5s) is insufficient to escape this local optimum вЂ” every order is dropped regardless of how feasible the time windows and travel times are.

The correct fix (for the production code, not the tests) is to add the disjunction only for the PICKUP node, since the pickup-delivery constraint already ensures the delivery is also dropped when pickup is: `routing.addDisjunction(new long[]{pickupIdx}, penalty)`. The two failing tests (`solve_singleOrderSingleVehicle_assignsOrderToRoute` and `solve_multipleOrders_respectsCapacityConstraints`) deliberately assert the correct expected behavior (orders assigned) and will pass once this production bug is fixed.
